title: Keiden: asking about several owners
summary: Ask about several owners with keiden/keitten: Keiden kirja tämä on? (“Whose book is this?”, several owners).
prerequisiteSkills: Adjective agreement in the singular genitive
objectives: Ask about several owners with keiden/keitten: Keiden kirja tämä on? (“Whose book is this?”, several owners).

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: The question word refers to the owner, not the number of objects. These questions all concern one object, shown by tämä on.
Kuka has the plural genitive keiden; keitten is also standard. Use it when the question explicitly concerns more than one owner.
Plural genitives can answer: lasten (“the children's”), opettajien (“the teachers'”). The question asks about the people, not whether they share one object.
keyPoints: Choose the question word from the owners' number.

steps: Use keiden/keitten to ask about several owners. kirja names the single thing owned.
